content:
maria: FYI support ticket #4578 — enterprise customer seeing p95/p99 spikes for long-context requests after yesterday's FalconX onboarding. They've been routed to the new model.

maria: Observed: normal traffic 1.2s p95 -> now 8s p95 and 18s p99 for sequences > 32k tokens. Affects only production region us-west-2 and dedicated pool fd-31.

devon: on it. any logs or trace ids?

maria: pasted the request id: req_20240902_01. stack traces attached in ticket. main symptom: tokenization step takes unexpectedly long after the first page. Repro curl below.

maria: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"falconx-extended-2024-09","input":"<very long document>...","max_tokens":1024}'
```

anika: interesting. new FalconX onboarding added a tokenizer variant (bpe-merges-v2) that normalizes CJK differently. I wonder if the tokenizer is producing pathological token counts for long sequences and causing K/V cache churn.

jon: I ran a quick synthetic against the same model on canary. Repro: sequences > 25k tokens, p99 jumps from ~3s to ~17s. CPU flame shows lots of time in tokenizer::decode and in kv_cache::evict.

devon: that matches K/V churn hypothesis. If tokenization produces more tokens than expected, kv cache gets invalidated more often causing repeated rewarm. Any change in default chunk size?

anika: yes — onboarding PR bumped bpe window from 2048 -> 4096 to improve split quality across languages. That increases avg token count for long inputs in some edge inputs since we now favor finer-grained merges.

maria: Customer is on dedicated pool; SLA breach risk. They asked for an ETA and mitigation.

devon: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Route the customer's traffic to the previous model build (falconx-2024-08) until we fix tokenizer. 2) Add a per-route shim to trim sequences > 30k (ugly). 3) Disable the new tokenizer variant via model config flag (preferred).

sre-bot: deploy queued: rollback falconx-extended-2024-09 -> falconx-2024-08 for fd-31. requested by devon.

devon: I'm going to prepare a rollback canary and a config toggle. Can anyone craft the minimal repro with curl + a smaller representative document so we can run in CI? Large docs hit storage limits.

jon: here's a reduced repro (same behavior):
```
{
  "model": "falconx-extended-2024-09",
  "input": "<repeat: lorem ipsum>" * 16000,
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```

anika: thanks. I'll instrument tokenizer to log token counts and merge-splits for this input. Also add metrics for kv cache evictions keyed by request id.

maria: customer agreed to temporary reroute. Please prioritize. They reported user-facing timeouts.

devon: deploy-bot shows canary rollback success on fd-31-canary. Can we confirm p95/p99 back to normal?

jon: after canary rollback p95=1.3s p99=2.9s for the reduced repro. I also verified dedicated pool fd-31-canary serves matching throughput.

anika: instrumentation shows token counts increased by ~28% with bpe-merges-v2 on certain unicode sequences — explains kv churn. Also noticed we compute full tokenization on the whole document before streaming starts, adding latency for first response when long docs are provided.

devon: two fixes proposed: A) revert merge-policy change and re-run onboarding with tuned merges; B) change runtime to allow streaming tokenization + incremental KV population (non-blocking tokenization). A is fast; B is medium-term but better.

maria: timeline request from customer: can we promise rollback until EOD?

devon: we already rolled router for their pool. Recommend keeping rollback and ship config toggle to disable bpe-merges-v2 globally until we validate. I'll open a hotfix PR.

anika: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/+/PR-6487 (toggle and metrics). Patch summary: add model_config.tokenizer.variant, default keeps old for current serving until verified.

sre-bot: hotfix PR deployed to staging: sha 3f9b2a1.

maria: customer updated — performance back to normal after reroute. They want a root cause writeup and assurance it won't recur.

devon: next steps: 1) postmortem doc draft with root cause + timeline, 2) run model onboarding validation harness against long-context corpora (multi-lingual + CJK heavy), 3) add an automated perf gate for tokenization inflation >15%, 4) plan runtime incremental tokenization work.

jon: I'll export traces and add them to the ticket. Also recommend we add synthetic monitors for sequences at different lengths so regressions surface earlier.

maria: thanks team. I'll notify the customer and keep ticket open until postmortem complete. :thumbsup:

devon: reassign to eng-runtime for follow-up; tagging @anika for tokenizer changes and @jon for monitoring work.

maria: closing loop later today with ETA for the postmortem.

(Reaction notes: several :eyes: and :shipit: reactions on the rollback messages.)
